newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks lock in another record close.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks lock in another record close.

text.p: Australian stocks bounded away in the afternoon to lock in another record close on Monday with the available investor interest clearly favouring the buy side.
The All Ordinaries Index added 15.2 points to 2,625.7, hitting a record high 2,626.0 on the way, surpassing Friday's previous high of 2,617.4.
Turnover was only moderate and buying interest was selective, with a strong preference for Friday's favourites, bellwether BHP and bank sector star ANZ Bank.
ANZ saw solid activity with 4.9 million shares traded and the stock ended up 2.9 percent at A$9.25 (US$7.03) after touching a record high of A$9.30. BHP rose 29.2 to A$19.15.
"ANZ is getting all the attention after its result last week and there is probably some switching in the group at the moment," said a dealer at a Sydney-based investment bank.

Where the broader impetus for the continued rally was coming from was unclear. Some suggested the old chestnut of Asian investors while others suspected the patchy moves were indicative of arbitrage activity remaining from last week.

"It could be some arbitrage activity but what I would call the real activity doesn't appear to be there to any extent. It's not wildly active," said Eric Gale, head of institutions at investment bank Ord Minnett.

Rio Tinto Ltd trailed its London shares lower, losing 18.1 cents to A$21.35. Shares in oil and gas group Cultus Petroleum NL dipped 15 cents to A$3.75 after it issued a statement saying that in its opinion recovery rates at the Cornea oil field offshore Western Australia were likely to be better than those indicated last week by joint venture partner Shell Australia Ltd, a unit of the Royal Dutch/Shell group.
Rises slightly shaded falls, while about 30 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
